verdict: WM's revenue rose 6.3% to $6.8B on 5.8% core price growth, and reported profit rose sharply against a year-ago quarter weighed down by a $213M impairment charge.

kpis.label: Returned to shareholders
kpis.note: $580M of buybacks plus $377M of dividends in Q3

segments.name: Collection
segments.note: Picking up waste from commercial, industrial, residential and other customers — WM's biggest line, helped by 5.8% core price growth.

segments.name: Landfill
segments.note: Fees for disposing of waste at WM landfills, including waste brought in by other haulers.

segments.name: Transfer
segments.note: Transfer stations, where waste is consolidated before longer hauls to landfills.

segments.name: Recycling Processing and Sales
segments.note: Sorting recyclables and selling the recovered commodities — the average recycled-commodity price rose to about $82 a ton from $68.

segments.name: Renewable Energy
segments.note: Turning landfill gas into renewable natural gas and electricity — growth projects completed since 2022 are now contributing, including a new New York facility opened this quarter.

segments.name: Healthcare Solutions
segments.note: Regulated medical-waste collection and secure information destruction (the former Stericycle business) — revenue up 3.7% with sharply better profit.

segments.name: Corporate and Other
segments.note: Small activities not run through the main segments.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Head-office and back-office running costs — 9.6% of revenue, better than last year's 10.3%.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion, amortization and accretion
opex.note: Spreading the cost of trucks, landfills and equipment over their working lives, including landfill accretion.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: Restructuring costs of $9M plus an $18M net loss from divestitures, asset impairments and unusual items.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $237M, partly offset by $2M of other income — a net $235M cost below operating income.
oneTimers: Reported profit includes an $18M net loss from divestitures, asset impairments and unusual items and $9M of restructuring costs; excluding adjustments, operating income was $1,329M and EPS was $2.15 (non-GAAP).
The year-ago quarter carried a much larger $213M impairment and unusual-items charge, which flatters this quarter's year-on-year profit growth.

takeaways.title: Pricing did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Revenue growth came mainly from price — core price rose 5.8% and Collection and Disposal yield 3.4% — while collection volumes slipped 0.4% as WM deliberately shed low-margin residential work.

takeaways.title: Healthcare Solutions swung to profit
takeaways.text: The medical-waste business lifted operating income by $41M year on year (to a $20M profit from a $21M loss) on 3.7% revenue growth, cost cuts and synergy capture.

takeaways.title: Cash flow funded big returns
takeaways.text: Nine-month operating cash flow rose 12% to $4.87B and free cash flow rose over 42% to $3.01B; WM returned $957M to shareholders in Q3 alone and affirmed full-year guidance.

footerNote: Chart layout adapts WM's printed statement: 'Operating' costs are the direct-cost block, and segment figures are net operating revenues by line of business from the Form 10-Q (intercompany revenues excluded). Net income is the $820M attributable to Waste Management, Inc.; noncontrolling interests were nil in the quarter.
